title: He looks like He’s losing.
paragraphs:
We love the empty tomb.
We celebrate the resurrection.
But we hesitate at the road that leads there.
Because Luke 9:23 doesn’t sound like comfort.
“Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me.”

Not once.
Not when it’s convenient.
Not when it’s trending.
Let me say it straight, kapatid.

Your cross is not your inconvenience.
It’s not traffic.
It’s not a bad mood.
Your cross is the place where your will collides with God’s will… and you choose Him anyway.

It’s when you want to reply in anger—but you stay silent.
It’s when temptation whispers—but you walk away.
It’s when pride rises—but you bow low.
But here’s the tension that breaks most people.
And that’s where many stop following.

Your secret habits.
Your hidden idols.
Your private compromises.
“Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.” — Galatians 5:24
Jesus never said, “Carry your cross alone.”
Before He ever commanded you to take up yours…
“But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
You’re not earning salvation by suffering.
You’re responding to a Savior who already finished the work.
That was love with a cost.

Your sin.
My sin.
Nailed there.
So when Jesus calls you to carry your cross…
He’s not calling you to pay for sin.
He’s calling you to die to the life that’s killing you.

That addiction you’re holding onto?
It’s not life.

That relationship pulling you away from God?
It’s not love.
That secret sin you keep defending?
Following Jesus will cost you something.

Friends may not understand.
Comfort will be disrupted.
Old versions of you will have to die.

A clean heart.
A clear conscience.
A real relationship with God.
“I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me.” — Galatians 2:20
You know exactly what God is asking you to lay down.

That habit.
That pride.
That hidden compromise.
The cross is not the end of your story.
“For if we have been united with him in a death like his, we will certainly also be united with him in a resurrection like his.” — Romans 6:5
So today, don’t just admire the cross.

Not in your strength.
But in His grace.
Because we don’t hide from the cross here.
And we follow the One who carried ours first.
